\begin{proof}
Let $N(p')=N(q')=X$, which is independent by
Lemma~\ref{lem:independent-neighborhood}(a).
Every other component of $B-X$ contains a vertex of $\{b,c,d\}$
and has a neighbor in $\{u,v\}$. None has neighborhood $X$,
by planarity of $B$.
There are therefore one, two or three such components.
We use the replacement argument and certificate checks preceding
Proposition~\ref{r2:ab-cut-outcome}.

Suppose first that one component contains $b,c,d$.
This component $D$ meets both $u,v$, since otherwise one has degree
two, and hence $N_B(D)=\{u,v\}$. Each test adds an edge from $a$ to $D$,
giving three bridges adjacent to all of $X$.
Contract the components of $D-\{b,c,d\}$ to a set $M$, retain a
spanning tree of $D$, and keep a minimal set of edges joining every
$m\in M$ to $\{u,v\}$ and $D$ to both $u,v$.
These operations preserve the connected interior and all four failures,
so minimality makes the reduction trivial.
A vertex of $M$ with only one tree neighbor would need both $u,v$.
Another vertex of $M$ supplies one of these adjacencies, making an
edge redundant. Thus the bipartite tree satisfies
$2|M|\le |M|+2$.
It is a star whose center is joined to $b,c,d$, or a path
$g_1m_1g_2m_2g_3$ with $\{g_1,g_2,g_3\}=\{b,c,d\}$.
For the star, its center meets both $u,v$, or one and a vertex of $\{b,c,d\}$ meets
the other. For the path, $m_1,m_2$ meet different vertices of
$\{u,v\}$, or both meet one and a vertex of $\{b,c,d\}$ meets the other.
The $31$ forms in~\supp{E12} leave exactly
$\mathfrak T_{40},\mathfrak T_{53},\mathfrak T_{56},\mathfrak T_{73}$.

vertex names: Psi_2 with twins p, q on {a, b, c} and r, z on {a, b, d}, as in Section 5. The bridge B has attachments a, b, c, d and contains u, v and the twins p', q' with neighbourhood X = {a, u, v}. The vertices of M are m (star) or m1, m2 (path g1 m1 g2 m2 g3).
the forms: One component D of B - X contains b, c, d, with N_B(D) = {u, v}. Its bipartite tree is a star whose centre m is joined to b, c, d, or a path g1 m1 g2 m2 g3 with {g1, g2, g3} = {b, c, d}. For the star, m meets both u, v, or one of them and a vertex of {b, c, d} meets the other. For the path, m1, m2 meet different vertices of {u, v}, or both meet one and a vertex of {b, c, d} meets the other. Up to symmetry this gives 31 forms.
the four tests: Lemma 5.3 with (n_c, n_d) = (2, 2): G is toroidal if and only if one of B + ac + bd, B + ad + bc, B + ab + ac + ad, B + ab + bc + bd is planar.
